# 0000. Podział na moduły domenowe

## Status

Proponowany

## Kontekst

- Driver D2 (ARCHITECTURE.md): zespoły Pricing i Catalog nie mogą się wzajemnie blokować przy wydaniu.
- Driver D4: nowi dostawcy frontendu (zespół B2B) muszą móc dołączyć bez przepisywania shella — wymaga docelowo wydzielonych, niezależnie wdrażanych modułów (np. Module Federation), do czego obecna struktura nie jest przygotowana.
- Driver D1: czas wdrożenia zmiany w regułach promocji musi spaść z ~3 tyg. do < 3 dni — wymaga możliwości niezależnego wdrażania zmian w module Pricing/Promotions.
- Context Map ([context-map.md](../context-map/context-map.md)) identyfikuje hotspot: `types.ts` to jeden płaski plik DTO dla wszystkich 14 bounded contexts ("brownfield anti-pattern" — komentarz wprost w kodzie), a `Promotion.productIds`/`Promotion.pricingRuleIds`/`WarehouseStock.productId` referują Catalog/Pricing przez surowe ID bez żadnej warstwy tłumaczenia (ACL) — sprzeczne z D2, bo zmiana kształtu modelu w jednym module może po cichu złamać inny.
- Dziś repozytorium (`retail-operations-portal`) to pojedyncza aplikacja bez wewnętrznych granic modułów — kod zorganizowany płasko wg typu pliku (`api/`, `store/`, `pages/`), nie wg domeny.

## Decyzja

Wprowadzamy podział kodu aplikacji na 4 moduły domenowe (modulith), odzwierciedlające 4 domeny z [context-map.md](../context-map/context-map.md):

- **`product-catalog`** — konteksty Catalog, Import/Export.
- **`product-pricing`** — konteksty Pricing, Promotions, Customer Segments, Validation Queue, Approvals.
- **`sales-fulfilment`** — konteksty Orders & Returns, Warehouse & Suppliers.
- **`platform/shared`** — konteksty Reports, Notifications, Audit Log, Identity/Users, Feature Flags.

Podział jest fizyczny w ramach jednej aplikacji (jeden `package.json`, bez npm/pnpm workspaces na tym etapie): każdy moduł to folder z jawnym publicznym API (np. `index.ts`) i prywatną implementacją; dostęp między modułami wyłącznie przez publiczne API, egzekwowany regułam

Confirmed by tracing every cross-boundary import: `src/app`, `src/layout`, `src/shared` already exclusively use the `@/app`, `@/layout`, `@/shared` aliases (no relative cross-imports, except one `../index.css` in `retail-operations-portal/src/app/main.tsx#L3`). So this is a **physical folder move + alias/config rewiring**, not a source-code rewrite — same pattern already used for the 4 domain modules on 2026-09-02.

## Plan: Move src/ (app shell) into packages/*

Relocate `src/app`, `src/layout`, `src/shared` into `packages/app`, `packages/layout`, `packages/shared` as three more modulith-style folders (same convention as the 4 domain modules — single shared `package.json`/tsconfig/Vite build, **not** real independent npm packages, per ADR-0000's explicit rejection of workspaces). `index.html` then points its entry script into `packages/app`.

**Steps**
1. `git mv`: `src/app` → `packages/app`, `src/layout` → `packages/layout`, `src/shared` → `packages/shared`, `src/index.css` → `packages/index.css` (kept as sibling of the package folders so `retail-operations-portal/src/app/main.tsx#L3`'s `../index.css` import needs no edit). Remove empty `src/`. Verify with `git status --short` (Windows has a history of stray duplicate files reappearing after `git mv` in this repo).
2. `vite.config.ts`: drop the blanket `'@': → ./src'` alias, add `'@/app'`, `'@/layout'`, `'@/shared'` → `./packages/{app,layout,shared}`. Keep `@/modules` and `@ross-org/*` untouched.
3. `tsconfig.json` + `tsconfig.app.json`: replace `"@/*": ["./src/*"]` with explicit `@/app/*`, `@/layout/*`, `@/shared/*` paths. **Critical**: change `tsconfig.app.json`'s `"include": ["src"]` → `"include": ["packages"]` — otherwise `tsc -b` has zero root files once `main.tsx` leaves `src/`, and the build would silently compile nothing.
4. `eslint.config.js`: update the 3  patterns (`shared`/`app`/`layout`) from `src/...` to `packages/...`. No policy logic changes — those types aren't referenced in any directional policy today.
5. `CODEOWNERS`: update the one `src/shared/` line to `packages/shared/`.
6. `index.html`: change script `src` to `/packages/app/main.tsx`.

**Relevant files**
- `app`, `src/layout`, `src/shared` — moved wholesale

- `eslint.config.js` — boundary patterns

- Modulith-style move only, no independent build/deploy for the shell (per your answers).

Two root causes, both in `experiments/workspaces/packages/my-lib/package.json`:

1. **No install has been run** — there's no `node_modules` under `experiments/workspaces`, so the npm workspaces symlink for the local package was never created.
2. **Invalid package name** — `"name": "myorg/my-lib"` contains a `/` but isn't scoped (doesn't start with `@`). npm package names can only contain `/` when scoped as `@scope/name`; `myorg/my-lib` is not a valid npm package name, so even after `npm install` it likely won't link/resolve as `myorg/my-lib`.

Fix: rename to `"@myorg/my-lib"` in that package.json, update the import in `experiments/workspaces/src/index.ts#L9` to `import("@myorg/my-lib")`, then run `npm install` at `experiments/workspaces` so the workspace symlink is created.

_**Agent (copilot/claude-sonnet-5)**_

Yes — npm scoped names just need an `@scope/` prefix:

```json
"name": "@myorg/my-lib"
```

Then:
- Update the import in `experiments/workspaces/src/index.ts#L9` to `import("@myorg/my-lib")`.
- Run `npm install` in `experiments/workspaces` so npm workspaces re-links the symlink under the new scoped name (`node_modules/@myorg/my-lib`).

No registry/publish step needed — scoping works purely locally for workspace-linked packages; the `@scope` is just part of the name, not an indicator it's published anywhere.
